compiled_state.description:
## Symptom

`scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py` refused a submit with:

```
refusing stale submit: Gerrit reports revision is no longer current
```

on a change whose revision *was* current. Gerrit's own detail endpoint reported
`current_revision = db3f3e396f1bb50a1350731cba30a6962d44fbaf`, `status: NEW`, two patch sets,
and that exact SHA as patch set 2 — the same SHA passed to `--revision`.

The real cause, from the POST body:

```
Cannot rebase db3f3e396f1...: Change 3169 could not be rebased due to a conflict during merge.

merge conflict(s):
* docs/release-notes.md
```

`GET /a/changes/3169/revisions/current/mergeable` confirmed `"mergeable": false` under
`REBASE_IF_NECESSARY`.

## Root cause

`scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py:130-146` wraps the submit POST and maps the whole of HTTP 409
onto one message:

```python
except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
    if exc.code == 409:
        print(
            "refusing stale submit: Gerrit reports revision is no longer current",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2
    raise
```

Gerrit returns 409 for several distinct conditions on submit, including an unmergeable change,
submit requirements not satisfied, and a genuinely superseded revision. The handler discards
`exc.read()` entirely, so the one condition it names is asserted regardless of which occurred.

The staleness check that *would* be authoritative already ran and passed at `:104-109`, comparing
`detail["current_revision"]` against `--revision`. So by the time the 409 arrives, staleness has
been ruled out — the message contradicts a check the same script just performed.

## Why it matters

The message points the operator at the wrong remedy. "Revision is no longer current" means
*re-inspect votes and re-submit*; a merge conflict means *pre-rebase and resolve*, which is the
documented exception to AGENTS.md's "do not pre-rebase" rule. Acting on the printed message
produces a loop of re-reading Gerrit state that cannot terminate, because nothing about the
revision is wrong. Diagnosis required dropping to a raw authenticated `curl` to read the body
the script had already received and thrown away.

This is also a silent-failure class: any future 409 condition is reported as staleness too.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1** The 409 handler reads the response body and includes it in the message, so the
      printed text names the condition Gerrit reported rather than a fixed guess.
- [ ] **AC2** When the body indicates the change cannot be merged, the message names the
      conflict and the remedy (pre-rebase and resolve), not staleness.
- [ ] **AC3** The script claims staleness only when it can show it — that is, when
      `current_revision` differs from `--revision`, which is already checked at `:104-109`.
- [ ] **AC4** A test drives the 409 path with a merge-conflict body and asserts the emitted
      message contains the conflicting path and does not contain "no longer current".
- [ ] **AC5** A test drives the 409 path with a genuinely superseded revision and asserts the
      staleness wording is still produced for that case.
- [ ] **AC6** Exit codes for the distinguished cases are documented in the module docstring.

## Evidence

Observed on change 3169 patch set 2 while landing `cb2b-7446-748c-47bc` on 2026-10-31.
The conflict was real and resolvable: a018 (`5cd7e2784ab`) and cb2b both inserted a new
section directly beneath the `docs/release-notes.md` header. Pre-rebasing and keeping both
sections cleared it.

## Out of scope

The conflict itself, and the adjacent-insert contention on `docs/release-notes.md` that
produces this class of conflict whenever two slices of one epic land close together.
